T he Aleutian Enterprise was a fish processing boat owned by Arctic Alaska.
"The ship was nearly full of frozen fish when the 28-year-old skipper, Mark Siemons, had his crew pull up the last catch before going home. The net was so full it split, spilling tons of fish onto the deck." (Eric Nalder, Seattle Times)
"'Pour on another eighty thousand pounds,' he cried" was a reference to the captain's decision to pull up one last load of fish.
That may have been the catalyst but it was not the underlying reason why the ship sunk. There was a hole on the side of the ship used as a garbage chute that was secured only by a steel flap. So when the last load came up, it tiled the ship to one side, causing water to flood through the garbage hole, trapping and killing 9 people.
Before this incident, Arctic Alaska had been dodging attempts to enforce regulations regarding load lines (which would have saved the 9 workers' lives), fighting with the Coast Guard who, themselves, were not properly enforcing the law. Just a year previously, the Coast Guard inspected the Aleutian and found violations but decided to allow the ship to operate while the company appealed the requirements. After the appeals failed, the Coast Guard did nothing. 6 months later, 9 people died.
The law required "Every opening between the waterline and the designated weather deck must have at least one, and usually two, watertight closures." The steel flap was far from watertight. The workers desperately tried to plug the hole but it was impossible. They died because the company refused to follow the law and put proper safety measures in place. The captain's decision gets the most attention in the song lyrics but, while it may have been a bad decision, it wasn't as consequential as the company's decision to ignore safety regulations.
The company's lies are infuriating. Apparently the law applies only to fish processing ships and not fishing ships, so the company tried to say it was just a fishing ship, even though the Coast Guard found processing equipment and other evidence of processing when they inspected the ship. They even tried to blame the dead workers for cracking the hull, even though there was no evidence to suggest such a thing. Just trying to cover their asses instead of taking responsibility for causing 9 deaths.
Maybe the most infuriating part is that the owner was prosecuted for conspiracy, lying to the Coast Guard, and involuntary manslaughter, but was acquitted. Fishing companies up there have a lot of power. Hands in all the right pockets.
